subject: Model tiering and context ramp playbook — kickoff and sizing
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ruth Park <ruth@finlytics.com>, Alex Ng <alex.ng@finlytics.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Model tiering and context ramp playbook — kickoff and sizing

Ruth / Alex — great to meet last week. As discussed, I want to pull together a concise onboarding playbook that maps model tiers to expected context lengths, token mix, and the 90‑day ramp for usage so your SREs and data platform team can size capacity and budget accordingly.

High level proposal (attached: playbook-overview.pdf + context_window_matrix.xlsx + token_ramp_estimates.csv):
- Model tiers: small (fast, quantized), medium (8–16k context), large (32k+ context)
- Recommended primary candidate per tier with fallback options (latency vs cost tradeoffs)
- Context window mapping by feature (search summarization, session chat, batch archive reranking)
- 90‑day token velocity scenarios (conservative / expected / aggressive)

Immediate asks for FinLytics team so we can finalize sizing:
1) A short list of feature endpoints you expect to go live day‑one (e.g., chat, document summarization, embeddings for similarity) — 1–2 lines each.
2) Typical context shape per endpoint (average document length, expected conversational turns, whether you plan to send full doc vs snippet).
3) Any strict latency SLOs per endpoint (p95 target).

Plan: we’ll take your inputs, populate the context_window_matrix, and return a per‑tier GPU footprint + cost row that your procurement team can use. Can we do a 30m sync tomorrow to run through the matrix? I’m available 10–11:30am PT.

Thanks — Jordan

Jordan Blake
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0132
Redwood Inference

Attachments: playbook-overview.pdf (9KB stub), context_window_matrix.xlsx (14KB stub), token_ramp_estimates.csv (6KB stub)

From: Ruth Park <ruth@finlytics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Ng <alex.ng@finlytics.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Model tiering and context ramp playbook — kickoff and sizing

Jordan — thanks, this looks good. A few quick clarifications before the sync: 

- Live day-one features: chat‑assist for customer support (session history ~10 turns), document ingestion + summarization for compliance reports (avg doc 12k tokens, but we often only send sections), and nightly batch reranking for alerts (batch sizes vary).
- For chat we target p95 <= 350ms for short prompts (<1k tokens). For summarization we can accept up to 1.5s p95.

A couple of asks from our infra team: can you model an intermediate tier (medium‑plus) for 24k context that balances cost vs dropping to full 32k? We expect a significant portion of our documents to be between 8–20k tokens and want to avoid full 32k hardware for all traffic.

We can do the 30m tomorrow at 10:30am PT — Alex and I will be on.

—Ruth

To: Ruth Park <ruth@finlytics.com>
Cc: Alex Ng <alex.ng@finlytics.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Model tiering and context ramp playbook — kickoff and sizing

Perfect — thanks for the detail, Ruth. We’ll include a 24k medium‑plus candidate and show the per‑request cost delta vs dropping to 32k for those larger docs.

Prework I’ll do before the 10:30am PT sync:
- Populate the context_window_matrix with your feature shapes and example doc lengths (attached).
- Produce three 90‑day ramp scenarios (Conservative / Expected / Aggressive) in token_ramp_estimates.csv with daily token projections and expected peak QPS.
- Provide GPU footprint rows for each tier (NVIDIA L4 / A10G class equivalents and estimated concurrency per device).

Agenda for the 30m sync (10:30–11:00am PT):
1) Quick review of FinLytics feature shapes (5m)
2) Walk matrix rows and confirm context lengths and fallback policies (10m)
3) Review 90‑day ramp and agree on an initial commit target + burst plan (10m)
4) Action items and owners (5m)

If anything else is helpful to surface to procurement before the call (SLA language, encryption-at-rest details, or example pricing for reserved vs hosted), flag it here and I’ll bring it.

See you tomorrow — Jordan

Attachments: context_window_matrix.xlsx (updated stub), token_ramp_estimates.csv (draft stub)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ruth Park <ruth@finlytics.com>, Alex Ng <alex.ng@finlytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2026 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Model tiering and context ramp playbook — kickoff and sizing

Jordan / team — quick note from ops: Ben and I sketched a fallback policy that we can discuss during the sync. Short version:
- If input >24k and latency budget <600ms, route to medium‑plus (24k) for first pass; if tokens still exceed threshold, send a trimmed prompt + metadata pointer and route to large (32k) async summarization.
- Cache recent KV for signed-in users to reduce repeated context costs (expected 12–18% token savings for support chat).

I added the policy as comments in context_window_matrix.xlsx. Minor ask for the call: can Jordan include a per‑tier example request/response trace (token counts + timing) so procurement understands unit economics?

Thanks — Grace
